convention: UNRESOLVED, treat with care: the FAO 1952 population series is sometimes far BELOW true total population (~1/3) and sometimes equal to it. Never treat a low figure as evidence of a territorial mismatch, and never treat this series as reliable total population — corroborate against a crop/livestock magnitude before drawing any territorial conclusion.
evidence: Below-total cases: Yugoslavia 1937-1947 median ~5.08M vs ~14-16M actual (1931/1948 censuses), with a similar ratio cross-checked against USA, Germany, Japan and the USSR — reading as agricultural/rural population. Turkey 1937-1951 median ~6,086k vs ~17-19M actual, the same ~1/3 pattern. Equal-to-total case (so far the only one): Saar 1937 = 821,000, matching the actual total (~812k at the 1935 plebiscite) — note the Saar is small and overwhelmingly non-agricultural, which may be the discriminator. So the series is not uniformly one measure; the split between the two behaviours is not yet characterised.

convention: IIA labels its Soviet series "Russian Federation" / "Russia" but reports WHOLE-USSR territory, not the RSFSR proper. Route to the USSR-scope polity; check magnitudes before ever routing such a label to a Russia-proper polity.
evidence: Cotton lint ~796k ha and cotton seed ~1.5M ha medians (1922-1940) are far too large for the RSFSR alone (Soviet cotton was grown in Central Asia and Transcaucasia); rye ~22M ha is union-scale.

convention: For pre-1945 years IIA's "south korea" label covers the WHOLE Korean peninsula (Japanese Chosen) — no separate southern entity existed. Anachronistic label, peninsula-scale data.
evidence: 432 dated rows 1909-1945 with peninsula-scale magnitudes; consistent with the IIA's colonial-era Korea coverage.

convention: For 1949-1960 the juan source carries a single undifferentiated "germany" label with no FRG/GDR split; route to the aggregate-Germany polity, not West Germany alone.
evidence: 603 rows across 11 years (1950-1960) under one label, no companion FRG/GDR series anywhere in the window.

convention: juan reports Finland on the settled post-1940 reduced-territory basis throughout 1941-1960 — it does NOT switch to the briefly recaptured Karelia borders during the Continuation War.
evidence: Sown-area series (barley/oats/wheat) smooth and continuous across 1941-1944 and the 1944 armistice; oats fall 472k ha (1939) to a 310k ha trough (1945) then recover — wartime disruption, not a territorial step.

convention: The juan/Mitchell-FAO compiled crop-area (and likely production) series under the label 'Czechoslovakia' are reported on a roughly constant, pre-Munich/post-restoration territorial basis across 1919-1946+; they do NOT reflect the 1938-1944 wartime territorial losses (Sudetenland, southern Slovakia, occupation) that CShapes documents for polity F51-1938-1945. Treat 1938-1944 'Czechoslovakia' rows from this source as best-available (not territorially verified) matches to F51-1938-1945.
evidence: Direct extraction of barley and potato area (ha) by year from the juan/Mitchell-FAO source file shows smooth values across 1937-1946 (e.g. barley 671k/660k/656k/754k/647k/659k/590k/549k/550k/546k for 1937-1946) with no ~28% step change at either the 1938 or 1945 territorial-change boundaries documented in the candidate polity's wiki page.
